key_insight: Across both spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells, efficiency loss during ageing is best explained by the mobility-lifetime product (μτ), not by lifetime alone.
engineering_relevance: This provides a single physics-based descriptor for predicting and comparing photodegradation in both lab-scale and scalable printed OSC manufacturing.
method: Compared PM6:Y12 spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed OSCs.
Tracked device performance during ~1000 h of continuous illumination.
Related degradation in PCE, mobility, lifetime, and recombination losses to μτ and morphology changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1000 h of continuous illumination and shows that despite different initial properties, PCE degradation systematically follows μτ, with printed devices showing higher lifetime but much lower mobility.
watch_item: A longer recombination lifetime does not necessarily mean better device performance; printed architectures may also include metastable dark-recovery behavior that complicates stability interpretation.
paper_title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
